title: Social Media Ad Sizes, Explained Simply | AIVideosUGC
description: A plain-English guide to social media ad sizes: when to use vertical 9:16, square 1:1 or wide 16:9 on TikTok, Instagram, Facebook and YouTube.
h1: Social Media Ad Sizes: Which Shape Goes Where
lead: Social media ad sizes come down to the shape of the frame: 9:16 for a full phone screen, 1:1 for feeds, and 16:9 for wide screens. Use 4:3 or 3:4 only when the placement lists that shape.
secondary_keywords: square ads for the Facebook feed
summary: Make 9:16 first for full-screen phone ads, add 1:1 for feeds, and make 16:9 only when the screen is wide.

sections.h2: How do I choose 9:16 vs 1:1 vs 16:9?
paras: Match the shape to the screen. 9:16 fills an upright phone, 1:1 sits in a feed, and 16:9 fits a laptop or a TV.

These are shapes, not pixel sizes. Pixel counts change by placement, so check the crop in the ad manager before you publish. 4:3 and 3:4 are available too. Use them only when that placement lists that shape. For the current Shorts file rules, see [YouTube Shorts ad specs](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/16041697?hl=en-GB).
sections.alt: Plain white sunscreen tube shown inside vertical, square, and wide blank frame shapes.

sections.h2: What vertical video ad size fills a phone?
paras: Use 9:16 so the product fills TikTok, Reels, Stories, and YouTube Shorts.

The caption runs along the bottom, and the like and share buttons sit on the right. Keep the product and any words you add in the middle. Cover the bottom and the right side of your phone with your fingers. If you can still see the product and read the offer, the frame is safe.
sections.alt: Adult woman with a short dark bob holds a plain white sunscreen tube in a tall phone-shaped composition.

sections.h2: What is the Instagram Reels ad size?
paras: Reels on Instagram and Facebook use 9:16, the same tall frame as Stories. Do not put the square feed file in that placement.
A wide file in that spot leaves empty bands above and below. Make the tall version as its own file. Cutting a landscape clip down afterward often crops the product.
sections.alt: Adult hand checks a plain white sunscreen tube inside a simple blank preview frame with generous margins.

sections.h2: When should I use square ads for the Facebook feed?
paras: Use a 1:1 file for the Facebook and Instagram feeds, and whenever you are not sure which placement will run.
It is also the usual shape for a carousel, and every card should match. A still of the same product at that square size can sit in the feed beside the video.
sections.alt: Adult Black man with short hair holds a plain white sunscreen tube centered in a square feed composition.

sections.h2: Which aspect ratio for TikTok ads fills the screen?
paras: TikTok in-feed ads use 9:16. A 16:9 clip on an upright phone shrinks to a thin band, and the product looks small.

Make that tall file as its own job with [AI UGC video ads](page:video-ads). Do not drop the wide version in and hope the crop keeps the product. Other lengths and tools are on the [AI video generator for ecommerce](page:video-hub).
sections.alt: Adult hand presents a plain white sunscreen tube in a wide horizontal tabletop scene.

sections.h2: Which social media ad size should I make first?
paras: Make 9:16 first. It covers the full-screen phone placements. Add 1:1 if you also run feed ads. Make 16:9 only when the viewer is on a wide screen.

Each shape is its own job. A finished clip does not switch shapes by itself. A 10-second clip is 40 credits, so a second shape costs another 40 credits, not another shoot. Keep the same photo and the same sentence, and change only the size. All five shapes can run 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds, at 24, 40, 60, or 120 credits. Do not slice a tall video down to a square in an editor. That often cuts the product off. [AI image to video](page:image-to-video) can rebuild the scene at the new shape from the same still.

Check the preview on your phone. A second shape is another job, the cost shows first, and a failed job returns the credits.

faq.q: Can one video work on every platform?
faq.a: It will not look right everywhere. A tall clip fills TikTok and Reels and gets cropped or shrunk in some feeds. A 9:16 version plus a 1:1 version covers most social spots.

faq.q: How do I keep text inside the safe area?
faq.a: Leave the bottom and the right edge clear for captions and buttons. Add the final words after you download, then check the preview in each ad manager.

faq.q: Does another shape mean filming again?
faq.a: No. Keep the same photo and the same sentence, pick the new size, and run a separate job. A 10-second video is 40 credits.

faq.q: Which length works with each shape?
faq.a: All five shapes can be 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds. Use 6 for one moment, 10 for a short demo, 15 for a simple sequence, and 30 for a longer one.
Only when the ad manager lists that shape. If it does not, stay with 9:16, 1:1, or 16:9. All five shapes are available.

faq.q: What mistakes make the ad look broken?
faq.a: Black bars from a wide file in a tall spot, a product parked on the edge that gets cropped, tiny text that only reads on a laptop, and trimming one shape out of another so the product loses a side.

cta_title: Choose the shape before you make the ad
cta_lead: Match one product scene to the frame it will play in, preview the crop, and download that version.
